Hi Olivia / Trevor —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and next steps from our side so we’re aligned: 

Call highlights:
- Primary objective: Reduce inference cost and latency for FinPay’s fraud scoring pipeline while keeping model outputs consistent with current baseline.
- Decision criteria: 1) ≤450ms P95 for 2k QPS, 2) <15% latency variance across regions, 3) SOC2 + formal procurement signoff.
- Timeline: Procurement expects to complete evaluation by end of December; you mentioned an internal steering meeting next week to confirm budget.

Attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that maps stakeholders, milestones, and owners — Redwood_MAP_Draft_v2.pdf. Key asks from your side: confirm economic buyer and procurement contact, and share any required security evidence checklist items we should prioritize.

Proposed next steps (suggested dates):
1) You confirm stakeholder roster (this week) — owner: FinPay (Olivia)
2) Redwood provides SOC2 + data flow diagram and updated SLA summary (Nov 12) — owner: Redwood
3) Tech validation workshop (Nov 18) — owner: FinPay + Redwood
4) Procurement terms review + redlines (by Dec 3) — owner: FinPay procurement

I’ve also added links to the HubSpot deal and a DocuSign placeholder for approvals at the bottom of the MAP.

If that looks good, I’ll update the MAP to reflect the stakeholder names you confirm and circulate an owner-responsibility column.

Thanks —

Marissa Cole
